title: Financing the EU budget: an assessment of five proposals for new resources
summary_en: How should the EU finance its next multi-annual budget? Darvas and Dom assess five proposals for new own resources: shifting 30% of ETS auction revenue, allocating 75% of CBAM revenue, a tobacco-excise levy (TEDOR), an e-waste levy, and a corporate resource for Europe (CORE). They endorse four with modifications and recommend the fifth (CORE) be scrapped, citing tax-design problems including cascading effects.
policy_relevance: Direct relevance for Hungarian EU-budget negotiations (KKM, NGM, EU Funds department) ahead of the 2028–2034 MFF. Hungary's net position depends materially on which own resources prevail: ETS- and CBAM-based resources favour high-emission economies (which Hungary partly is), while a CORE-style corporate levy would hit Hungary's FDI-dependent industrial base disproportionately. Useful negotiation playbook input.
